instructions: Fill a large pot with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk the 6 tbsp tahini with 4 tbsp of the sesame oil until smooth. Whisk in the 2 tbsp light soy sauce, the 1 tbsp dark soy sauce and the sugar. It will be thick.
Whisk in warm water 1 tbsp at a time until the sauce is loose enough to pour. That should be about 3 tbsp.
Mince the garlic. Slice all 4 scallions thin. Chop the cilantro until you have about 1/2 cup. Chop the mustard stems and the pickled long beans so you have 1/2 cup of each.
Cook the noodles in the boiling water for 1 minute less than the package says, so they stay chewy. Drain well, shake off the water, and transfer them to a large bowl.
Toss the noodles with the remaining 1 tbsp sesame oil so they don't clump.
Add the sauce, mustard stems, long beans, garlic, scallions, cilantro and the black vinegar. Toss quickly for about 30 seconds, until every strand is coated.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the noodles among 4 bowls. Serve with the chili oil on the table.
To pack it for lunch, keep the noodles in the fridge for up to 2 days. Toss with a splash of warm water and eat at room temperature or warmed in the microwave.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so this follows the best-rated one, The Woks of Life (4.89 from 17), doubled to serve 4. It builds the sauce from tahini, sesame oil and two soy sauces, tosses it through short-cooked, oiled noodles, and tops it with preserved mustard stems and pickled long beans. My Spicy Kitchen builds a looser sauce with hot water and adds cabbage, carrot and chicken, which this version leaves out. Chili oil goes on the table so the base stays mild. Look for the mustard stems (zha cai) and pickled long beans at an Asian grocery.
